name: Open models
blurb: Open-weight LLMs: model and licence choice, VRAM maths, Ollama and llama.cpp, vLLM, RunPod and Modal, GGUF, LoRA fine-tunes and evals.
searches: open-weight LLM agent skill Ollama llama.cpp vLLM new
fine-tuning skill LoRA QLoRA TRL Unsloth agent
GGUF quantization imatrix new quant types llama.cpp
self-host LLM RunPod Modal serverless vLLM skill
open model licence commercial use Llama Qwen Gemma change

tests.prompt: I have a MacBook Pro with 32 GB of RAM. What's the best open coding model I can run locally with Ollama, and how do I hook it up to my editor?
tests.good: Does the memory maths (weights about parameters x bytes x 1.2 plus KV cache at the real context, with headroom, and macOS needing its share of unified memory) and suggests a size class that fits at Q4_K_M or Q5_K_M rather than a bigger model at Q2; checks the licence on the card; pins an explicit tag, not :latest; sets num_ctx in a Modelfile instead of relying on the default; notes Ollama's MLX backend applies only above 32 GB; smoke-tests and reports tokens per second from eval_count and eval_duration; gives the OpenAI-compatible base URL http://localhost:11434/v1 for the editor and keeps the server on localhost.

tests.prompt: We want to stop paying per token and host Llama 3.3 70B ourselves for an internal support tool. Can we use it commercially, and how do we run it on a rented GPU?
tests.good: Reads the Llama Community Licence terms (acceptable-use policy, Built with Llama, naming, the 700M monthly-user threshold, gated access) and says gated is not restricted; does break-even maths from GPU price per hour and measured tokens per second; sizes 70B for weights plus KV cache and picks a GPU shape or quant (AWQ or tensor parallel) accordingly; chooses vLLM with --max-model-len set; on RunPod uses a network volume, HF_TOKEN from env, --terminate-after or workers-min 0, and async calls on cold start; keeps the endpoint authenticated; verifies health, a real completion and load from outside; ends with a list command showing nothing left running.

tests.prompt: Fine-tune Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on our 3,000 support tickets so it answers in our house style, then give me a GGUF I can run in Ollama.
tests.good: Asks whether prompting or retrieval would do first and scores the base model on a held-out 10% split; converts tickets to messages format without editing the original and validates columns; uses LoRA or QLoRA with all linear targets, alpha = 2r, a LoRA learning rate, effective batch under 32 and bf16; uses current TRL names (processing_class, max_length) and assistant_only_loss with plain TRL since Unsloth lacks it; picks a runner and sets a teardown on paid GPUs; merges into the full-precision base, converts and quantizes to Q4_K_M with llama.cpp, imports via a Modelfile with the right template; re-evaluates the GGUF for gain and regression; notes the fine-tune inherits Qwen's licence.

tests.prompt: Build a customer-support agent that runs on our own open model instead of a paid API: it should look up orders through our REST API, and we want to deploy the whole thing with Docker on our server.
tests.good: States the plan first: open-models for the model end (choosing-models-and-licences.md for a tool-capable model and its licence, vram-and-sizing.md, serving-endpoints.md for vLLM or llama-server on localhost, agents-and-tools.md for base URL from env, tool calling and validated arguments), ai-agents for the agent itself (tool-design.md for the order-lookup tool's name, schema and errors; frameworks.md; evaluation.md for an eval set run against the local model and the current API), cloud-devops for docker.md (model server and agent containers, GPU access, model weights on a volume, no keys in the image). Keeps the model server private; checks the Done means of all three crafts and says what wasn't verified.

tests.prompt: I already run Ollama on my Linux PC (RTX 4090) with a few models pulled. I want a ChatGPT-style web page my family can use from their laptops and phones on our home Wi-Fi, each with their own login and chat history, and I don't want to lose everything when I update it. Set it up.
tests.good: Runs the official image ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main with docker run -d -p 3000:8080, a named volume mounted at /app/backend/data and --restart always, and sets WEBUI_SECRET_KEY (for example from openssl rand -hex 32); reaches the host's Ollama correctly from the container with --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway and OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:11434 rather than localhost or 127.0.0.1 (which is the container itself), or with --network=host noting the UI is then on port 8080, and only sets OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 on Ollama if it is actually needed; creates the admin account straight away because the first account to sign up becomes the administrator; handles family accounts with the user roles: new sign-ups default to pending (DEFAULT_USER_ROLE) and the admin approves them, or the admin creates the accounts and turns sign-up off (ENABLE_SIGNUP=false), and does not use WEBUI_AUTH=False since that is single-user mode; notes that settings such as ENABLE_SIGNUP, DEFAULT_USER_ROLE and connection URLs are persistent config, so after the first start the values saved in Admin Settings win over environment variables (unless ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=False); updates by pulling the new image and recreating the container on the same volume so accounts and chats persist, and verifies from another device on the Wi-Fi at http://<pc-ip>:3000 that the Ollama models are listed and a chat works.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.why: Most-starred project in the space (about 182k GitHub stars) and the default easy local runner in the 2026 round-ups from pinggy.io and openalternative.co.

tools.name: llama.cpp
tools.why: About 130k GitHub stars; the engine under Ollama, LM Studio and Jan, with the broadest hardware support (pinggy.io, openalternative.co round-ups).

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.why: Named as the desktop-GUI choice for non-terminal and Windows users in the 2026 round-ups (pinggy.io, openalternative.co); ships an lms CLI, a headless llmster daemon and an OpenAI-compatible server.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.why: About 93k GitHub stars; named the production serving standard for concurrent users in the 2026 round-ups and comparison posts.

tools.name: Hugging Face Hub (hf CLI, transformers)
tools.why: The default registry for open weights: over 1M transformers checkpoints and the model-definition layer that vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp and Axolotl read (Transformers docs); official hf CLI, Jobs and an official MCP server.

tools.name: Unsloth
tools.why: About 77k GitHub stars; ranked first for single-GPU speed and lowest VRAM in the 2026 framework comparisons (spheron, MarkTechPost, dev.to EVAL #003).

tools.name: TRL (Hugging Face)
tools.why: About 19k GitHub stars; the framework of choice for DPO, GRPO and other alignment beyond SFT (2026 comparisons); Unsloth and LlamaFactory build on it.

tools.name: RunPod
tools.why: One of the two GPU hosts named in the guide's own sources; official skills, an MCP server (hosted and npm) and a CLI; widely used for rented-GPU pods and serverless vLLM.

tools.name: Modal
tools.why: Serverless GPU platform used for vLLM endpoints and training jobs; one of several equals to RunPod, HF Jobs and Vast.ai.

tools.name: SGLang
tools.why: About 37k GitHub stars; the main alternative to vLLM, offered as an engine by Hugging Face Inference Endpoints and Unsloth.

tools.name: Axolotl
tools.why: About 12.5k GitHub stars; the YAML-driven, multi-GPU reproducible-pipeline pick in the 2026 fine-tuning comparisons (spheron, MarkTechPost).

tools.name: MLX LM
tools.why: About 7k GitHub stars; Apple's own Python package for generating, quantizing, serving and LoRA-tuning on Apple silicon.

tools.name: lm-evaluation-harness
tools.why: About 14k GitHub stars; the standard academic benchmark runner behind the Open LLM Leaderboard style numbers.

tools.name: Open WebUI
tools.why: About 154k GitHub stars; the usual self-hosted chat front end for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible servers (openalternative.co and pinggy.io round-ups). Promoted to major by the critic: 2026 round-ups describe Ollama plus Open WebUI as the very common setup, and at about 149-154k stars it out-stars every other tool here except Ollama.

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.why: Unified API to 300+ models, most of them hosted open weights; the usual way to try an open model before renting a GPU; official skills and a remote MCP server.

tools.name: LlamaFactory
tools.why: Most-starred fine-tuning framework (about 75k GitHub stars, ahead of Unsloth, TRL and Axolotl); 2026 comparisons call it the most popular by raw numbers, with a web UI (LlamaBoard) and CLI covering SFT, DPO, KTO, ORPO and PPO. It was left out only because the guides already cover it, which ranks by gap rather than by use.

tools.name: Google Colab
tools.why: Hosted Jupyter with free and paid GPUs; the default place practitioners run their first fine-tune: Unsloth's 100+ official notebooks target Colab (and Kaggle) first, and Unsloth now drives Colab GPUs from VS Code. The guides never mention it.

tools.name: Together AI
tools.why: Listed first among open-source LLM hosting providers in 2026 round-ups (edenai, siliconflow): OpenAI-compatible serverless and dedicated inference for open models plus hosted LoRA/full fine-tuning and GPU clusters, i.e. the managed alternative to the craft's serve and fine-tune jobs. Official MIT skills exist.

tools.name: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM
tools.why: One of the three serving engines every 2026 comparison names beside vLLM and SGLang (highest throughput on standardised NVIDIA clusters, FP4 on Blackwell); serves OpenAI-compatible endpoints via trtllm-serve. NVIDIA NIM is NVIDIA's packaged route. Absent from serving-endpoints.md.

tools.name: Weights & Biases
tools.why: Long-standing standard for training experiment tracking (loss curves, hyperparameters, GPU metrics, sweeps); Transformers, TRL, Unsloth, Axolotl and LlamaFactory log to it with report_to="wandb". Now part of CoreWeave. The guides only mention trackio.
